policy: The v1.6.7 contract is frozen: each active source's URL building, list parsing and JD fetch live in jobs_scraper/sources/<source>.py, and sg_product_jobs.py keeps only thin wrappers over them — one implementation per behaviour, verified by AST. The active CLI sources are linkedin, jobstreet, cake and 104/onezerofour; jora stays retired from active crawling and is kept only for back-compat dedup of historical rows. Every source adapter's list fetch retries a transient 429/5xx/connection/JSON failure with a 30/60/90s ladder (four attempts), raises any other 4xx without retrying, and never retries a legitimately empty page; a run counts as successful only when the list crawl actually produced pages, because an empty crawl exits 0 by design. A legitimately empty LinkedIn list page is 26 bytes and yields no parseable root: the list parser returns zero jobs for it instead of raising, so one empty page can never end a page loop, a chunk or a run. The LinkedIn JD fetch uses the same 30/60/90s ladder (four attempts) for a 429, a 5xx or a connection error, and does not retry any other 4xx, because a job whose JD never arrives is skipped by the Sheet writer and would otherwise disappear from the run silently. Code that generates a Python worker embeds its arguments as Python literals, never as JSON: json.dumps(None) is the bare token null, an undefined name in Python, and such a worker dies before it reaches Google and silently costs the run the subprocess timeout guard that protects the Sheet write. A generated worker never carries the jobs payload in its source: the payload travels in a separate JSON file the worker reads, because a source that embeds it grows to megabytes and makes CPython pull the whole literal through its tokenizer before the write can start, which is a memory spike on a machine whose free-page count is already in the tens of megabytes. The engine's title filter, Sheet write order, cross-source identity, work-mode values and single-source-of-truth crawl state are unchanged by this release; future source expansion or retirement requires an explicit authorized contract change. Outbound proxy resolution lives in one place, jobs_scraper.sources.resolve_proxies(), and every adapter that talks to a third party uses it: JOBS_SCRAPER_PROXY first, then the standard HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY, and nothing set means a direct connection; no source may reach for a proxy variable of its own. The doctor reports which proxy is in effect and probes whether it is still reachable, because a configured-but-dead proxy fails every source at once. China is three crawlable places, not one: the China region is Shanghai, and Hangzhou and Shenzhen are their own regions with verified LinkedIn geoIds in the LinkedIn adapter's preset table. A region resolves its Sheet tab through a tab-base rule, so the two city regions land on China-Raw / China-Selected together with the China region, and the expected-tab list is de-duplicated so the initializer never creates a shared tab twice; the city regions stay opt-in and the default region set remains SG / TW / China. A China posting carries no visa judgement: China-specific citizenship wording produces no signal, because a Taiwan resident can take a permit into mainland China. The generic coverage stays — a Singapore or Taiwan posting that requires any citizenship is still a hard blocker, and the Singapore-only gate on the Sheet's visa column is unchanged. The pre-detail dedup reads the tab the run is about to write to: the target gid is resolved with the same precedence the writer uses — explicit --gid, then the #gid= inside --to-sheet, then the source-label mapping — and it is threaded into the loader, into the generated worker and into main(); a label-to-gid table alone is not a target, because LinkedIn / Minimax points at SG-Raw, so a China run compared its postings against Singapore's tab and paid for a JD fetch round the writer was going to discard. With no target given, the label-to-gid mapping still applies, so the Singapore and Taiwan flows behave exactly as before, and an explicit target is authoritative without needing a known label. A range's page budget must cover the pool that range actually has in every known city, not only the city it was measured in first: the LinkedIn budgets are pinned to the deepest measured pool per range across Shanghai and Singapore, and the JobStreet budgets are pinned to the totals the JobStreet API states for itself, sized for the largest keyword's pool plus headroom — the JobStreet daterange parameter takes a number of days, mapped through JOBSTREET_TPR, never the CLI range name. No budget ever shrinks and no time filter ever changes. The Guest API refuses to paginate past start=1000: it answers HTTP 400 rather than an empty page, so a budget beyond 100 pages buys nothing and a crawl that asks for an unreachable page ends with what it collected instead of aborting — the ceiling is an end, not a failure, and a supervisor never reads it as a coverage gap. A non-429 4xx on a LinkedIn list page is raised immediately as FatalListPageError, exactly as the JobStreet adapter does, because the retry ladder is for transient failures and a caller bug only burns the backoff ladder.
